name: Member, San Francisco Board of Supervisors

budget.basis: 2025-26 · Citywide annual budget, all funds, adopted by the Board in the two-year appropriation ordinance and signed by the Mayor (July 2025)

constituents.basis: 2020 Census count for San Francisco (873,965) divided by 11 supervisorial districts. The Redistricting Task Force used an adjusted redistricting total of 874,933 and reported an ideal of 79,545 per district.

jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco

powers.value: The Board is the legislative branch of the City and County: it introduces and adopts ordinances and resolutions through committees, and it adopts the city's budget (appropriation) and salary ordinances after the Mayor proposes them. Under Charter section 1.101, powers not given to another officer or body are reserved to the Board.

term_limit.value: Two four-year terms in a lifetime, whether or not consecutive (Proposition B, approved June 2, 2026). Before that, Charter section 2.101 barred more than two successive four-year terms, with a four-year wait before returning; a partial term of more than two years counts as a full term. A transition clause lets sitting supervisors, and those elected June 2, 2026, finish their current term.

notes: Budget and Appropriations Committee chair: Connie Chan has chaired the committee since February 2023 (sf.gov About District 1, primary, search summary). Its 2026 members were Chan, Dorsey, Sauter, Walton and Mandelman (sfbos agenda bac061026, primary). The Mayor's proposed two-year budget and the Annual Appropriation Ordinance for FY 2026-27 and 2027-28 were received June 1, 2026 and assigned to the committee. The committee holds department hearings and public comment, negotiates changes with the Mayor's office, and sends a recommended budget to the full Board. Per news summaries, the June 2026 committee deal reversed about $28.5M of proposed cuts (SFist, June 26, 2026), and the Board President credited the Budget Chair with the negotiation. Charter section 2.100 has the Civil Service Commission set supervisor pay every five years, with CPI-U annual adjustments capped at 5%. The May 18, 2026 materials propose $180,128 for FY 2026-27 (+2.7%, effective July 1, 2026); I found no record of the final vote. An opinion column gave $170,430 as of July 2024. CONFLICTS: The FY 2026-27 budget was reported as $16.9B, approved unanimously July 21, 2026 (GrowSF citing the SF Chronicle, secondary, unverified). In 2025 Axios reported the plan as $16.3B for 2026-27. Board file o0190-24 (the prior cycle) showed about $15.57B for FY 2025-26. Prop B (June 2026) reportedly passed with about 53% (Mission Local). Mission Local reports that some attorneys say November 2026 Prop A could undo it; the City Attorney says Prop A does not change term limits. A June 30, 2026 Board resolution (file 260753) reportedly declared the results; I did not see it. Seat count of 11 is implied by the redistricting materials, not quoted. Scott Wiener's 2011-2016 tenure comes from the maintainer and was not re-verified. graph.civlab.org could not be fetched (host blocked), so no CivLab data was seen for this office; secondary coverage says CivLab's San Francisco GovGraph maps SF entities and budgets.
